newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish key rate seen steady to March - survey.
newsitem.headline: Finnish key rate seen steady to March - survey.

text.p: The Bank of Finland's tender rate, its chief monetary policy tool, is expected to remain unchanged with few operators seeing a rise from the current 3.00 percent in the next three months, according to a Reuters poll.

Of 21 analysts, dealers and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments, 19 expected the tender rate to remain unchanged at 3.00 percent. One saw the rate at 3.25 percent at the beginning of March, while one expected it to be raised to 3.50 percent.
No one anticipated a cut in the tender rate. The forecasts ranged from 3.00 percent to 3.50 percent and the median was 3.00 percent.
Looking one year ahead, the tender rate forecasts ranged from 3.00 percent to 4.50 percent and the median was 3.50 percent.
Sixteen participants out of 21 saw the tender rate in a 3.00-3.50 percent range. Of these, two expected it to remain steady at 3.00 percent.
One respondent expected a hike to 4.50 percent.
The quarterly poll was conducted on Thursday last week. Forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.

Forecasts by: Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), S-E Banken (Helsinki), Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
